[~accountid:5cfa2e89757e4b0f2636ebf7] I discussed this with Anni and she confirmed the following:

* She confirmed that the Risk & Safety team is not able to support the temporary solution (using a 7-year block instead of hard-blocking) and therefore it is CS leads that would need to keep track of these users themselves.
* In high priority events where we’d apply this 7-year scheduled block solution in place of the hard-block, agents can:
** include a specific phrase (like “_7-year block applied”_) in the Description of Event field in the Assessment Tool 
** and then select Yes to confirm they took the suggested action (hard-block) - because theoretically, we are hard-blocking, just with a different action, so there’s no need to select that a deviant action was taken
* She recommended not tracking anything on a separate Google Sheet since we already keep data on hard-blocked users from what is logged in the tool. Instead, she recommended that Darina Kurakina can instead do the following when we need to check up on the users who were “hard-blocked” with the 7-year scheduled block:
** utilise the Carsharing dashboard to which she has access, to filter any hard-blocked users from a certain date for this check
** Alternatively, Darina can simply check all hard-blocked users for the Speeding reports process (because we will know that once the temporary solution is enabled for the Speeding reports process, all users who were “hard-blocked” will have the 7-year block applied on their user account. 

The above details clarify everything for me. Since this Jira task actually goes on about the hard-blocking instructions for Car misuse HP events (speeding reports is not one of them - we discussed the speeding process because they share the topic), I’ll create a separate Jira task (with 0.5 story points) to complete the update for the Speeding reports KB article. 👌

The following principles should be followed:

* Obvious best practises when it comes to localisation (keeping style, grammar and vocabulary consistent)
* It is important to ensure that the localised self-help version matches the source text provided (EN-US), this includes:
** Exact information provided
** Formatting (bullet points, bold, punctuation, hyperlinks/underlines)
* Word by word translation is not the goal, it is more important that the localised text flows naturally in the local language without undergoing any factual changes.
* *Note:* If you detect any factual mistakes in the source text or have other content suggestions, do not edit your localised version. Instead, leave your notes in the designated cells in the sheet

Addressing the DSAR submitted on 02.02.2022. This was submitted by e-mail which contained details of the person whose personal data should be disclosed. Per our KB [procedure|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360021283220--Driver-Requests-Their-Data], in case of an email request (and not in-app), the identity of the person should be verified first. Therefore I suggest the following response to the requester:

_Dear Mr Kawani,_

_We are in receipt of your data subject access request submitted 02/02/2022._ 

_Firstly, we want to address the following information which has been requested by you - confirmation that you are processing my personal data; the purpose of your processing; the categories of personal data concerned; the recipients or categories of recipient you disclose my personal data to; your retention period for storing my personal data or, where this is not possible, your criteria for determining how long you will store it; confirmation of the existence of my right to request rectification, erasure or restriction or to object to such processing; confirmation of my right to lodge a complaint with the ICO or another supervisory authority; information about the source of the data, where it was not obtained directly from me; the existence of any automated decision-making (including profiling); the safeguards you provide if you transfer my personal data to a third country or international organisation._

_Please note, that if you have used our software services under the General Terms for Drivers, your personal data is being processed in accordance with Bolt’s Privacy Notice for Drivers accessible here_ [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/legal/gb/privacy-for-drivers/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/legal/gb/privacy-for-drivers/]. _Furthermore, information in regards to all of the questions listed above can be found in the Privacy Notice referred._ 

_Secondly, you have requested a copy of your personal data and provided details in e-mail which includes the name, address and e-mail address which should be used to identify the data subject. However, in order to disclose any personal data, Bolt as the controller of the data needs to make sure it really is the person who owns the account by verifying the data subject. The procedures on verification are in place first and foremost for the user’s own security. For that we ask the verification of identity by providing the selfie with holding the official document issued by the government. The procedures on verification are in place first and foremost for the person’s own security and to ensure that the disclosure is made to the named data subject - i.e. you - and to safeguard against the unlawful disclosure to any other third party._

_Therefore we ask to verify your identity in order to proceed with the data subject access request._ 

_Best regards_

Hey there Gaspard. 

Those markings are fraud indicators that were triggered by our fraud rules. We have hundreds of fraud rules and some of them do markings on the orders, such as these. Repetitive orders, as the name indicates, show repetitive rides by a parameter that can be device, ip, user, email, etc. You don’t have to take any action when you see those flags in an order, we do it on our side with other action rules. 

In this case, seems the driver was trying to cash out this driver campaign [https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet_campaign/Campaign/campaign/99596?period_id=846256|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet_campaign/Campaign/campaign/99596?period_id=846256]

If you open the orders and take a look, you’ll see that they’re fake short rides (1-2min) with the same user that would help the driver reach the campaign goals faster. Those are pre-arranged rides controlled by the driver, he either owns the rider account or he’s in contact with the person who’s controlling the user.  

Here are a few order examples:
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865574362/963502413|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865574362/963502413]
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865573368/963500897|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865573368/963500897]
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865575188/963503764|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865575188/963503764]
[https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865577628/963507915|https://westeurope-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/865577628/963507915]

As you can see, those are not legit orders. Due to the fraud flags, we prevented the driver from exploiting the bonus. Those rides that were flagged didn’t count towards the campaign goals. 

In addition to the driver campaign, the user also had campaign discounts. So those rides were also an attempt to cash out rider campaigns.

Hi Mihkel, good morning. I'm the Data Protection Risk Manager at Bolt and I'm here to answer some questions and reinforce some items regarding what has already been correctly said by Liis.

First of all, regarding GDPR, we need to know *exactly what are the purposes of your project involving this vendor*. I don't know if this has already been told to Liis, but as I just entered the conversation, I saw that the purpose is this: "_Begin scheduling and timekeeping system to use for Estonian mechanics team and in-house OPS team for Tallinn_". And this is not very clear, especially regarding the following items: _What personal data will be used? For what purpose? How long will the personal data be stored? Where the personal data will be stored? Will there be any other purposes for the use of this data?_ These questions are essential because Bolt can only use personal data if there is a clear and specific purpose, and this is not clear just from the sentence indicated above.

Second, the data protection management process *does not start with a simple analysis of a contract*, but with the analysis of the level of risk to personal data - this is why Liis mentioned the likely need to perform a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) concerning your project. This is mandatory under the GDPR, especially when there are elements that, it seems to me, are present in this project: automated decision making with legal or similarly significant effects; systematic monitoring; sensitive data or data of a highly personal nature; data processed on a large scale (due to the number of employees that may be subject to this personal data processing activity); and also data concerning vulnerable data subjects (employees in this case). This DPIA, it seems to me, will be mandatory *even if biometric data are not used*, as indicated by [~accountid:5b4490ccd09e562c1b7b5592] . But I can only be sure after the basic questions presented above are pointed out to us, and the project can only move forward if it passes this DPIA, because without it Bolt (and the project manager) could be held liable.

Third, we can only transfer personal data to a new vendor if there is a contract (and, as Liis rightly pointed out, what was passed on to us is not a contract as required by the GDPR) and we also need to have some knowledge regarding the vendor's existing security mechanisms. This is relevant because *Bolt is responsible for the personal data during the whole life cycle of the project*. This means that if there is a problem with any vendor handling the data on behalf of Bolt, the responsibility will not lie with the vendor, but with Bolt. In addition, Bolt needs to know which are the subsequent vendors, if any (i.e., vendors subcontracted by the original vendor).

Finally, I emphasize that our job is to protect the personal data of our clients, first and foremost, but also to protect Bolt and those responsible for each project started at Bolt. If there are problems with personal data under Bolt's responsibility (or under the responsibility of any vendors contracted by Bolt), the company could pay up to *20 million euros in fines*. Furthermore, I emphasize that Privacy Legal's role is only to *make recommendations regarding the best options for projects*, but *the final decision regarding "go" or "no-go" is up to the project owner*. Therefore, for us to assist you in the best way, I kindly ask you to fill out the questionnaire available at this link: [https://www.cognitoforms.com/BoltTechnologyOÜ/PreliminaryPrivacyRiskAssessment.|https://www.cognitoforms.com/BoltTechnologyO%C3%9C/PreliminaryPrivacyRiskAssessment.] After filling it out we will come back here with an indication of the next steps concerning the DPIA. If you have any other questions, I remain available.

*NB\!* This experiment takes into account only documents that were rejected only due to one reason — a mismatch of the driver’s license number. If this and expiry date change are both added it would affect more documents.

I use a Levenshtein distance value to ensure that two values are _‘almost’_ equal.

I highlighted with {color:#36b37e}green{color} OCR values that have only 1 character that does not match the manually entered value.

And with {color:#ff991f}orange{color} values with 2 symbols mismatched.

_The invoice information for transactions between non-VAT taxable persons is regulated by the Law on Accounting, Article 13._

# _Document name (“invoice”)_
_Document date_
# _The name and code of the issuer of the invoice. We understand that this provision should be read as follow:_

# _Description of the transaction_
_Value of the transaction_

The law allows not including the signature on the invoice if the accounting services are being provided by the accounting service provider and it is agreed that the signing requirement would not be applied. # _Company name, registration number or taxpayer’s registration code;_
_For private individuals – name, surname taxpayer’s registration code;_
+*_If the buyer is a private individual not performing a business activity – Name and surname._*+

* it seems like {{IllegalVoipRepoStateException}} is indeed benign and does not affect ASR, it's because of multiple "Answer Call" taps - reporting for multiple taps can be prevented in app in the future, but right now its fine to live with it.

* Acquiring Push token failed error - seems like this is on the Sinch side, probably Sinch cannot communicate with FCM correctly, might be connected to 401, but it's better to ask Sinch, it is low priority
* There are `SinchPushExceptions` errors which might be connected to not synchronised clocks between caller and callee, needs more investigation, but the assumption is that we cannot fix it, timestamp checks are likely {{a feature}} on the Sinch side, I will follow up on that with Sinch
* We have now some data about network quality. We should compare it to TIMEOUT result and if we can see some correlation lets ask Sinch if we can for example extend TIMEOUT duration on demand

So far the analysis is done and it will be reiterated as a separate task when CA.35.0 is released and adpopted.

Propose to address creation of settings records with eventual consistency in mind.

Provider table to have additional field {{provider_app_settings_state}} ({{not_initialized}}, {{initialized}}).

When creating provider via admin panel, optimistically attempt to call endpoint that creates settings (handling all errors in try-catch).

If attempt fails, {{provider_app_settings_state}} remains {{not_initialized}}.

Lifecycle to have cron that finds {{not_initialized}} records in small-ish batches and attempts to create app settings for them.

App settings creation endpoint should be idempotent (upsert) in case of desync ({{delivery-provider}} thinks creation failed, but it did not).

Unfortunately, with the (potentially) async nature of this, strict validation logic for any future fields we want to add will have to live in Lifecycle’s admin panel logic.

A bonus that we get out of this is that we won’t need to run a data script to initialize settings for existing providers - we’ll just let the cron do its job for a certain period.

The {{provider_app_settings_state}} field can later be used to determine whether certain settings are available in the admin panel and perhaps whether the provider can log into the app (no such blocking settings exist at the moment).

{code:sql}WITH _payment_problem AS (
SELECT
	payment_id,
	created,
	state,
	RANK () OVER (PARTITION BY payment_id
ORDER BY
	created DESC) AS rnk
FROM
	fraud_user_payment_problem
WHERE
	created >= DATEADD('month',
	-1,
	CURRENT_DATE)
	AND state <> 'ignored'
GROUP BY
	1,
	2,
	3
),
card_age AS (
SELECT
	o.id AS order_id,
	o.city_id AS city_id,
	o.user_id AS users,
	COALESCE (fc.card_country, 
	pmu.card_country) AS card_country,
	COALESCE (fc.card_age_in_days,
	fc.user_created_age_in_days) AS card_age
FROM
	company_order AS o
LEFT JOIN company_order_try AS ot ON
	ot.city_id = o.city_id
	AND o.id = ot.order_id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_order AS po ON
	po.city_id = o.city_id
	AND po.order_id = o.id
	AND po.type = 'order'
LEFT JOIN payment_payment AS p ON
	p.payment_order_id = po.id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_row AS pr ON
	pr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_user AS pu ON
	pu.id = po.payment_user_id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS pmu ON
	pmu.payment_user_id = pu.id
	AND pmu.payment_method_id = p.payment_method_id
	AND pmu.payment_method_type = p.payment_method_type
LEFT JOIN pii.etl_archive_analytical_user_order_request_data AS fc ON
	fc.id = o.fraud_calculation_id
	AND fc.user_id = o.user_id
WHERE
	ot.state = 'finished'
	AND o.payment_method_type <> 'default'
	AND o.created BETWEEN DATEADD(MONTH,
	-1,
	CURRENT_DATE) AND CURRENT_DATE
           ),
_driver_bad_payments AS (
SELECT
	o.country
,
	ot.driver_id
,
	DATE_TRUNC('month', o.created) AS order_created_month
,
	COUNT(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN o.id ELSE NULL END) AS count_of_bad_payments
,
	COUNT(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN o.id ELSE NULL END)* 1.0 /
NULLIF(COUNT(o.id), 0) AS bad_payments_count_percentage
,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ca.card_country <> o.country AND (pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error')) THEN o.id ELSE NULL END) AS foreign_card_bad_payment_count
,
	COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ca.card_country <> o.country AND (pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error')) THEN o.id ELSE NULL END)* 1.0 /
   COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN o.id ELSE NULL END) AS foreign_card_bad_payment_count_percentage
,
	SUM(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN pr.amount / r.rate ELSE NULL END) AS amount_of_bad_payments
,
	SUM(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN pr.amount / r.rate ELSE NULL END)* 1.0 /
NULLIF(SUM(pr.amount / r.rate), 0) AS bad_payments_amount_percentage
,
	AVG(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN ot.distance ELSE NULL END) AS avg_bad_payment_pickup_distance
,
	AVG(CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR (pr.type = 'chargeback' AND pr.state = 'finished') OR (bub.uncovered_amount>0) OR (oa.id IS NOT NULL AND pr.TYPE = 'capture' AND pr.state = 'error') THEN ca.card_age ELSE NULL END) AS avg_bad_payment_card_age
FROM

In case we still decide in favor of it, we are allowed to sell only non-prescription medicine via distance sales.

Please find the detailed answer of the external counsel below.

----

*Food supplements* fall under the generalized category of food, thus, no special licenses are required (besides product’s registration with the Food and Veterinary Service). However, we advise checking the registration of the food supplements intended for sale in the [Food supplements register|https://registri.pvd.gov.lv/en/ub], otherwise the food supplements may be confiscated by the authority.

The requirements for selling medicines differ depending on their type:

 Retail sales of *prescription and non-prescription medicines* requires a +pharmacy license+, which can be obtained in accordance with the Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 800 [“Procedures for the Licensing of Pharmaceutical Activity”|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/238458-procedures-for-the-licensing-of-pharmaceutical-activity].

Such a license requires registration with the State Agency of Medicines and a physical pharmacy to be established which conforms to the requirements of the [Pharmaceutical Law|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/43127], Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 288 [“Regulations Regarding Operating of Pharmacies”|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/207397-regulations-regarding-operating-of-pharmacies], Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 610 [“Criteria for the Location of Pharmacies and Pharmacy Branches”|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/234279-criteria-for-the-location-of-pharmacies-and-pharmacy-branches] and the aforementioned Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 800 [“Procedures for the Licensing of Pharmaceutical Activity”|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/238458-procedures-for-the-licensing-of-pharmaceutical-activity].

Furthermore, only *non-prescription medicine* can be sold remotely (through a distance sale) and the pharmacy license must contain a special condition allowing such. The requirements for obtaining a special condition are:

# the possibility for the buyers to communicate with the pharmacy via the website during working hours and to receive free of charge information and consultations from the abovementioned medicinal products in the provision of pharmaceutical care in accordance with the laws and regulations regarding the requirements for the opening and operation of the pharmacy;
# a website that is established in accordance with the 

      [Law On Information Society Services|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/96619-law-on-information-society-services], which is accessible to the buyer at any hour of the day without    interruption, and the information posted therein conforms to the laws and regulations regarding advertising of medicinal products;

3. notification to the Health Inspectorate and the State Agency of Medicines of the date when the remote sales will begin, the website used and the e-mail address of the seller.

These requirements must be fulfilled by the seller of goods (Bolt Market). The law sets no special requirements for the delivery of medicines, however, they must be transported in such a way that does not render them unsuitable for use.

We suppose that it is currently impractical for Bolt Market sellers to obtain pharmacy license. However, products like food supplements, bandages, band-aids, pregnancy tests, thermometers and similar may be sold without pharmacy license, so perhaps you might wish looking into this direction. If the product is classified as _medical device_ then additional rules may apply (there are different classes of medical devices, each with different rules), but it would nevertheless be more feasible than a pharmacy license.

In terms of the retention schedule- as collecting this information is not a regulatory obligation, from legal perspective there are no specific prescribed timeframes when the data should be deleted.

However one of the core GDPR principles is that personal data shall be kept for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed. Therefore, personal data can be kept as long as the processing purpose reasonably applies, but data should not be kept indefinitely “just in case”, or if there is only a small possibility that it will be used.

In other words, you have to assess from business perspective what should be appropriate average lifespan of this data and for how long this information will be reasonably used.

There are some key points to address in your response to the passenger (which apply to all of our communications):

(1) We must avoid making any statement that suggests we acknowledge that we are responsible for a loss (such as “you _were_ overcharged”). This impacts our ability to convincingly suggest otherwise at a later date.

(2) We must avoid saying “we do not provide refunds”, even if our policy is to not provide refunds (at first instance or ever, whether partial or full). It’s not a justifiable reason to refuse compensating someone for an overcharge. Statements like this will foreseeably annoy/frustrate any customer and influence them to escalate matters further.

(3) We should not tell customers who they should contact in the event of a dispute escalating. There is no need for this customer to have any involvement with an ombudsman to issue a legal claim. We should stick with our arguments and leave it to customers to seek their own legal advice. 

Dealing with any formal claim made by any person is a colossal cost / time-sink for Bolt. Any time a formal claim is made, I will spend several hours dealing with it and Bolt will spend hundreds, if not thousands, of pounds, on external legal fees making it go away (even if we are completely in the right legally). In other words, the costs of refusing a refund grossly outweigh the costs of providing a refund.

Because of our response to date (points 1-3 above, which we do not want anyone else to have visibility of, especially not a court) this is definitely not something we want a claim being issued on. I suggest a full refund is made promptly, PLUS giving the customer the benefit of Bolt credit, even if this causes Bolt a loss.

cl 3.4 - Bolt will not accept any additional costs. cl 4.2 and 4.3 - no offer will be accepted unconditionally. Bolt and GfK will negotiate an offer which is suitable for both parties, which consequently will be agree to in writing by both parties. 

cl 4.6 - again, each and every purchase of the service is based on the offer which is mutually agreed to in writing by both parties. No partial obligations or estimations raise any obligations and neither of them are relevant if clearly stated that only in writing agreed offer becomes binding. 

cl 5.1 - no unilateral amendment of the service and fees is acceptable. 

cl 6.2 - please rewrite. Only direct damages

During card payment instrument deletion {{findPendingPaymentForPaymentMethods()}} checks for unfinished (≈pending) payments. According to [the SQL query logic|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/559a5f621f6c847fa21c20d7417aca9e445865a4/src/platform/payment/payment/main/table/payment.ts#L718-L722], any payment with the last action of {{CAPTURE}} in {{created}}, {{working}}, {{pending}} or {{error}} state would block deletion of the card. It looks like the idea behind it has been to catch successful authorisations that have not been captured yet. However, it also includes unsuccessful zero-auth payment attempts, because these are stored as successful authorisations followed by one or more failed captures. In the case of auto-retry, the card cannot be deleted until the retries are exhausted or stopped.

h3. PRELIVE statistics as of 07.03.2022

*06.03*
total payments: 1405664
payments with unfinished capture: 20861 (1.5%)
payments with unfinished capture and zero-auth: 16381 (1.2% of total, 78.6% of unfinished capture)

*04.03—06.03*
total payments: 4695900
payments with unfinished capture: 51103 (1.1%)
payments with unfinished capture and zero-auth: 41364 (0.9% of total, 80.9% of unfinished capture)

Based on the statistics, we can see that around 80% of the deletion declines due to unfinished capture actions relate to the failed zero-auth payments. Those should not be considered pending and block card removal.

I have to disagree with the information you got locally.

Wolt as a local entity must meet the local invoicing requirements of Croatia.



But, according to VAT directive article 219a, (2a), Bolt EE should meet the invoicing rules of the Member state where it has established its business - Estonia. Further to this, article 226 (11a) establishes that “reverse charge” should be mentioned on the invoice.

So our invoices for commission issued from Bolt EE to Croatian restaurants should not need to meet any further requirements.



The story is, however, different in the cases of self-billing - in this case, Bolt is issuing invoices in the name and on behalf of its suppliers (restaurants/couriers/drivers) to itself, charging compensations, bonuses, delivery fees. That’s why I asked you to send me an example of an invoice that we issue as self-billing - for these, we should comply with local requirements and I would like to see what we are currently doing.



Thx,

Helena

LOCKS=$(mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -N -e "SELECT COUNT(1) FROM information_schema.innodb_trx trx WHERE (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(trx.trx_started)) > 1;")

if [ $LEN -gt $MAX_LEN ] || [ $LOCKS -gt 0 ] ; then
  DIR=$DIR/$(date +%m-%d)
  if [ ! -d $DIR ]; then
    mkdir $DIR
  fi
  TIME=$(date +%H-%M-%S)
  mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -e "SHOW FULL PROCESSLIST" >  "$DIR/$TIME-$LEN-PS.TXT"
  mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -e "SHOW ENGINE InnoDB STATUS\G" >  "$DIR/$TIME-$LEN-STATUS.TXT"

  if [ $LOCKS -gt 0 ] ; then
    mysql --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -e "
      SELECT
        trx.trx_mysql_thread_id,
        trx.trx_mysql_thread_id thd_id,
        ps.user,
        ps.host,
        trx.trx_query,
        (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(trx.trx_started)) open_time_sec
      FROM
        INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INNODB_TRX trx
        JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PROCESSLIST ps ON trx.trx_mysql_thread_id = ps.id
      WHERE
        (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(trx.trx_started)) > 1
        AND user != 'system_user';" > "$DIR/$TIME-$LEN-LOCKS.TXT"  
  fi
fi

According to the driver, the fleet is denying that they received any amount.

However, if we bake DAGs into the image we will have to restart each component on each release. It’s not an issue with the scheduler and webserver. 

With CeleryWorker, the graceful shutdown will allow tasks to finish (with reasonable timeout). During the shutdown, it won’t accept any new tasks, so we will need to spin up a new worker while deploying. So each deployment will result in increased costs.

Of course, having more than one worker has benefits and should be considered for critical sites - however, it might not be required for all of them.

The above table describes temperature range for the work place, but is not tailored to situations, where the main place of work would be in cold rooms or where most of the working time is spent in cold rooms.

*Risk assessment by labour protection specialist*. If employees must regularly work in cold rooms / freezers, additional work environment risk assessment must be carried out pursuant to Articles 17 and 18.2. of 2 October 2007 Cabinet Regulations No. 660 “[Procedure for internal monitoring of the working environment|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/164271-darba-vides-ieksejas-uzraudzibas-veiksanas-kartiba]”, since the work environment risks change. Usually, such assessment is made by labour protections specialists based on the changes in work environment and work conditions. The main additional work environment risks in case of work in cold rooms are rapid changes in temperature (if employees must work in cold rooms and other premises, where temperature is different) and work in cold (if employees work mostly in cold rooms) and other risks if such risks are identified by labour protection specialists.

*Protective equipment for working in the cold rooms*. Where employees are required to work in cold, additional labour protection and work safety measures must be implemented. 20 August 2002 Cabinet Regulations No. 372 “[Labour Protection Requirements When Using Personal Protective Equipment|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/65619-darba-aizsardzibas-prasibas-lietojot-individualos-aizsardzibas-lidzeklus]” provide that in case of work in cold rooms and freezers in food industry, employees must be ensured with the following protective equipment:

* For hands - gloves to protect against cold;
* For feet - protective footwear against cold;
* For all or part of the body (including head) - protective clothing against cold.

Labour protection specialists will be able to recommend the best special protective equipment, considering the cold rooms that will be used and considering the changes in work conditions. +Based on Article 28(4) of Labour Law, Bolt will be responsible for ensuring labour protection and work safety and thus must organize provision of protective equipment to employees.+ It can also be agreed that this equipment is provided by the employer of the rented workforce, whereas Bolt compensates expenses related to such equipment use.

*Additional training (briefing) for pickers*. Since the use of cold rooms will result in change of work environment risks for employees, it is mandatory to organize unplanned briefing (instruction) fort the employees about working in cold rooms / freezers pursuant to Article 24.2 of 10 August 2010 Cabinet Regulations No.749 “[Training in Labour Protection Matters|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/214922-apmacibas-kartiba-darba-aizsardzibas-jautajumos]”. Such briefings are usually carried out by the contracted labour protection specialists based on the work environment risk assessment. Such instruction shall provide information about working in cold, effects of cold on body and signs of frostbite, other impact of cold on employees’ health, the use of protective equipment and guidelines to mitigate the risks associated with work in cold. After such briefing, the employees must sign for being instructed in a journal.

*Time spent in cold rooms and warning signs*. In addition to the use of protective equipment, the employees should be provided with possibility of warming up in the workplace to avoid employees working in cold rooms all of the time. Appropriate warning signs must be used for cold rooms, e.g. “Low Temperature” signs at the freezer doors.

*Additional health check for pickers*. Furthermore, it must be noted that all employees, who conduct 50% or more of their working time in premises, where temperature is below the table provided above, must be sent to mandatory initial occupational health check before commencement of work and to routine health checks every 3 years of work pursuant to 10 March 2009 Cabinet Regulations No.219 “[Procedures for Compulsory Health Checks|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/189070-kartiba-kada-veicama-obligata-veselibas-parbaude]”. Such occupational health checks must be organized and paid by the employer of the rented employees. Covering of such costs is subject to agreement between Bolt and the workforce service provider.

Hi Liis,

Thanks for getting back to me\!

To answer your questions:

# {color:#36b37e}*What exactly is this program about?*{color} We're aiming to increase our number of women drivers across all markets. We know women have different needs and challenges than men drivers so we want to have a number of initiatives that will make them feel more confident driving with us and show them that this can be a career for them too.
# {color:#36b37e}*What are the experiments we wish to conduct?*{color} The biggest initiative we want to do that will segregate drivers on the basis of sex is the Women-only category in ride-hailing where riders can choose their driver based on sex and maybe vice-versa. We're also making a big marketing campaign that targets women directly and we need to measure whether we managed to attract the female category or not.
# {color:#36b37e}*Would this be a global approach?*{color} Yes it is, countries in the pipeline for pilots are: Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Lithuania, Estonia and maybe also Czech R and Poland.
# {color:#36b37e}*Would we also ask for the gender of existing drivers as well?*{color} Ultimately we'll probably have to if we have no other way to guess ourselves. For example in some countries we know their sex based on a digit in their ID number, or we can probably determine based on their name but in some countries we have no other way so might need to ask directly.



I think we will have to add "I wish not to answer" however these will likely not be able to have the women-only category. Our biggest concern in this program is bias on the LGBTQ+ community which we want to be sensible about but not sure yet how we can make them feel comfortable too that they are being considered, mostly non-binary. 

Please note that in certain countries we are already tagging drivers on Admin if they are women but we do this manually and internally. If we want this to scale everywhere, the field would be useful and for example to be included in Step 2 of the registration asking Male, Female, Prefer not to say.



Another question the marketing team had was whether we could ask people's gender when we run ads on Facebook and share a google form to get their information?



Finally it would be worth reviewing if the women-only category is something we can do globally. Because we want to avoid asking gender to riders too, some few ideas out there are (only for the women only category):

#  to use rider face verification
# send like a “snapchat” of the rider to the driver so they can decide whether to take the ride or not
# have a pop up that warn riders that the driver is allowed to cancel on them if they are not women

Let me know your thoughts.

Thanks,

Karina

Hey\!

According to POPIA section 26 (similarly to GDPR) there is a general prohibition on processing special personal information (biometric data and criminal behaviour data). Section 27 states that the prohibition on processing personal information, as referred to in section 26, does not apply if the processing is +carried out with the consent of a data subject.+ 

Therefore, consent is still required to carry out this background check based on fingerprint checks. 

POPIA defines consent as voluntary, specific and informed expression of will in terms of which permission is given for the processing of personal information. +Therefore, consenting to privacy policy as such would not be deemed as specific and informed expression of will.+ 

How the current process would change -> drivers would not go to the TRA centre for checks anymore and Bolt would ask TRA to conduct the check and TRA will share with us the results. 

There are two ways to approach this:

# TRA must get a consent from the driver to conduct the criminal background check and to share this with Bolt (as it is right now) or 
# Bolt gets the driver’s consent to authorise a third party (TRA) to conduct the criminal background checks. +In the light of the proposed process, this would make more sense.+

My suggestions taking this together:

# Bolt will be the one asking for the consent for conducting the check (as drivers don’t go to TRA anymore). 
# Amend the consent form so that this does not cover only the checks during onboarding, but the annual checks as well (during the period which the drivers provide services on Bolt Platform.) 
# Amend the consent form so that it also informs about the payment obligation (will drivers start paying this fee to Bolt or still straight to TRA)?

Let me know your thoughts (and if I missed anything) and I can help drafting the consent form.

* 400: Validation error. It means the request did not contain enough data points or in an invalid format and that ProcessOut cannot understand the API request.
* 404: The resource could not be found.
** This one will happen in multiple cases where you are trying to either leverage or fetch a resource that does not exist.
** Ex: Requesting a authorization with a card ID or invoice ID that can’t be found.
* 409: This one is used for conflicts. For example when you try to do an authorisation, it hasn't yet finished and you try another action or the same it will return that.
* 410: This one would be any generic error (i.e. invalid API keys, errors coming from the PSP/APM etc..)

Hey\!

*Gifting scooters to the local municipality* – can be considered bribe, grease payment etc. Has extremely bad optics, media coverage can be negative and possible future implications (barring from procurement, criminal liability) significant. Imho, cost to benefit ration does not justify this approach.

*Business account, 0 fee* *_–_* risks are more hidden, but they are still there. On the whole, our operation _must_ be legal and _appear_ to be legal. This is something that can come back after a while and bite us.

*Business account, adjusted market fee* – discount from the current price list. Risks for Bolt minimal, but local municipality _might_ need a public procurement for this. The risk and optics can be handed to the other party - if they don’t follow the law or don’t have the justification for the agreement, it is mostly their problem.

*Direct contract, fixed fee* – same as above.

*Public Procurement –* done by the book, the least risky option.

 

Possible workarounds:

# Personal accounts and the expenses are reimbursed?
# Personal accounts and credit is given to the test group every week?
# Personal account, fixed discount and expenses are reimbursed?

Afaik, there are regulations regarding the reimbursement of expenses related to transport (taxi, public transport, rail, bus etc). This could be one of the possible solutions - the officers are using the scooters for fulfilling their tasks and should be eligible for compensation. Should this come into focus, they can state that they are gathering information for future actions and allowing officers to use the scooters, compensating them for the rides _and_ they can use Bolt, Jungo etc. If sufficient feedback is received from the officers, a tender for the upcoming years can be done.

+*Setup and test:*+ [~accountid:60717fb420947c006983e2d7] , I have added some additional steps that were not discussed earlier. 

* Need 2 drivers.
* Set default parameters from admin for both the drivers.
** Event: Driver Search Category Selection
** Params: {{{"is_driver_pricing_enabled" : true}}}
* Set default parameters for rider.
** Event: Drivers Selection and ranking.
** Params: {{{"driver_pricing": { "enabled" : true}}}}
* In the driver app, go to App Settings and you should see pricing methods, if not then go to the company of the drivers in the admin panel and mark {{Is fleet company = no}}
* Set *Your own price* from the pricing method in the driver app for both drivers.
* Set the lowest price for one driver and the highest for the other driver. 
* Keep the driver (driver A) with the lowest price online and the other (driver B) offline.
* Create an order that matches driver A and wait. Do not accept the order.
* When the rider is waiting for approval from driver A, make driver B online. 
* Since A doesn’t respond, the order goes to B who has a higher price. 

+*The logic used in client:*+

* When polling returns order state as {{confirmation_required}} we display a bottom sheet with the content provided by BE (in this case, price change). 
* After some time if the user still doesn’t respond, polling returns state as {{confirmation_expired}}. We dismiss the bottom and treat this order as failed and call {{getFailedOrder}} which returns the content of the dialog shown in the user’s screenshot. 

+*Investigation notes:*+

*  The logs look fine, there are traces of {{confirmation_required}} been sent from polling for approx 32 seconds, and then it returned {{confimation_expired}}
* We can notice that there is been some changes in the primary bottom sheet’s launch w.r.t router factory. 
* Have tested the scenario with both mocks and real-time. It works as expected. Screen recording for confirming, expiry, and cancel attached bellow.
* Since the ticket is old we can currently assume that it got fixed in the router factory changes and keep an eye if it gets reported again. cc: [~accountid:5f23e70bb7a35e002a73ef5d]

query to analyze resolved prebalance failed payments



{noformat}select cover_p.id good_pay_id,
    cover_r.type as cover_type,
       cover_r.state as cover_state
from
    payment_payment cover_p
    join payment_payment fail_p on fail_p.id=cover_p.previous_payment_id
    join payment_payment_row cover_r on cover_r.id = cover_p.last_payment_row_id
    join payment_payment_row fail_r on fail_r.id = fail_p.last_payment_row_id
    JOIN payment_payment_order as o ON (o.id = fail_p.payment_order_id)
where
    o.type != 'balance'
  and
    fail_r.last_update > DATEADD('month', -6, CURRENT_DATE)
  and (fail_r.type = 'capture' AND fail_r.state = 'error' OR fail_r.type = 'expire') --failed{noformat}

However, this only applies if the nicotine pouches have specific concentration level (high) in the product. Given that nicotine in nicotine pouches does not contain pure nicotine but the mixture of substances, it is hard to tell whether these concentration levels in these products trigger this requirement. To have a clear understanding of this, official legal opinion should be requested from the [Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre|https://www.meteo.lv/en/lapas/about-centre?&id=1473], including data about specific product (-s). Hey again,

If you receive a ticket from a user where they ask to delete their account due to an issue on our platform, *and it is clearly stated that they want to delete the account*, we should follow the process as usual.

Of course, we can try solving the user’s issue first by asking further information and/or asking them if they still wish to proceed with their account deletion. However, if we do it, we must ensure that we still action the deletion on time, which is 30 days from the request. 

Unfortunately, in Beehive, if we put the ticket to Pending, it will be closed in 5 days if there’s no reply from the user. Thus, if you ask the user if they still want to delete their account, you need to remember that the ticket exists. I don’t recommend putting those tickets as pending as it might go to the closed state and you can forget about it, but it is up to you how to action those tickets (e.g. the CS agent or TL can set a reminder etc) as long as the account deletion process is correctly followed.

*So, in conclusion: yes, we can try solving the user’s issue first. But unless they confirm that they do not want to delete the account anymore, we must proceed with the deletion within 30 days and cannot forget about the request.*

To avoid the risk of us not actioning on those requests, we have decided not to edit the process and leave it as it is. We’ll include the L&D team to see if we can educate agents on this with a training though, but if this happens, you’ll be notified via the relevant channels. 

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Eliise

We must be able to determine the weak points in accordance with HACCP principles. There are set requirements for frozen foods, chilled foods and hot foods, with allowable deviations from the base temperature.

From the Board of Agriculture:

_Toidu vedamine on üks oluline etapp toiduohutuse ning lõpptoote kvaliteedi tagamise seisukohalt. Toiduveol peavad käitlejad täitma kindlaid hügieeninõudeid, puhastama ja pesema sõidukeid ning veoruumi, tagama vajadusel kindla õhutemperatuuri veoruumis, mis on sobilik toidu transportimiseks. Sellisel juhul jõuab tarbijateni või edasiste käitlejateni nõuetekohane toit nõuetekohasel temperatuuril._

Translation:

_Transporting foodstuff is an important step in ensuring safety and the quality of the final product. During food transport, handlers must comply with certain hygiene requirements, clean and wash the vehicles and the loading compartment, and, if necessary, ensure a certain air temperature in the transport compartment that is suitable for transporting foodstuff. Doing so ensures that the right food reaches consumers or downstream operators at the right temperature._

Hey,

Bolt Balance uses the currency of the country where the user was located (at the time they received a refund). If the user travels to another country with a *different currency*, then unfortunately, they won’t be able to user their balance. 

Their balance will be saved (but won’t be visible in the app while they’re abroad) and they can use it as soon as they return.

Just to mention that we should issue a refund *using the same ride the user reached out to us about.* E.g. if the user had an issue with their ride in NO, we shouldn’t issue a refund using their ride in another country, e.g. in NL instead (a ride they didn’t have an issue with). 

Unfortunately, this is how it works at the moment, and it is not sure whether it is planned to change it at some point. If the Bolt Balance team plans to change it, we’ll let you know 🙂 If it is a big issue in your market, you may also give feedback to them directly about this, maybe they can do something or at least they know it is an issue in some countries. 

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Eliise

Hey there Anton. Thanks for escalating and sorry for taking so long to get back to you. 

You’re probably aware, as you were involved in deactivating tips in Kyiv, but just in case, here’s the document from the analysis Daria ran related to tips => [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3756490765/Fraud-risk+based+tips|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3756490765/Fraud-risk+based+tips|smart-link] 

As mentioned in the article, the next step is to analyze the business case for sub payments. Sub payments would cover all these cases where the final price is different from the preauthorized amount, either by a tip, by a wait time fee, a longer route that exceeds recalculation threshold, a toll fee that wasn’t predicted, or any other price change that impacts the ride price. Once we get an idea of how big is the business case, we can think and propose solutions for our devs to implement. 

Since the tip analysis already proved to have a relevant business case, makes sense that the sub payments will be way better, as it will include all other scenarios. Therefore, it will be certainly prioritized\! Hopefully, we can already have a solution for this huge old problem in Q2. With the balance flow, now we have more options to fix this sub payments issue, but it’s still WIP, one step at a time.

In a few words, we’re aware and we’re working on a fix. On a brighter note, despite the problems we have, fraud rates are still under control globally.

-the debt collection process is very much controlled by the agency; you don’t have much influence

-they cannot represent you at court, so if they are not successful you have lost time and need to instruct a lawyer anyway. 

*Option 2: Order for Payment Procedure*{{ }}*An order for payment procedure is a quick and simplified alternative to normal legal proceedings. The German order for payment procedure consist of two steps: It begins with applying for an order for payment with the competent court. This application is not comparable to a detailed statement of claim – you can use a standard form. The competent court only assesses if all formalities are met and issues an order for payment which the debtor will receive. It is then up to the debtor to react to this by either (i) paying the debt, (ii) objecting to the order for payment or (iii) remaining silent. In the event of an objection by the debtor, normal legal court proceedings follow. In the event of failure to act, an enforcement order may be issued. If the defendant objects to this, again normal legal proceedings follow. If he remains inactive, you will receive an enforcement order which is equal to a court ruling and which enables the actual debt recovery.* 

Pros:

+ Useful if you believe that the Order of Payment impresses the debtor enough so that he will finally pay. You are then much quicker than in normal court proceedings. 

Cons:

- If the debtor objects (which can be done very easily) then we will have lost time until normal proceedings start. 

*Option 3: Normal court proceedings*{{.}}*An order for payment procedures only makes sense if it is to be expected that the debtor either will pay upon such formal order received from a court or if it is likely that he remains silent. If you expect the company to refuse the return of the payment and to object to the whole proceeding then it may be recommendable to directly proceed with normal legal proceedings before the competent civil court. Normal court proceedings will take between 6-12 months.* 

If the relevant amounts aren’t low then the external counsel recommends starting normal court proceedings instead of using debt collection agencies and instead of starting this special Order for Payment Procedure.Lawyer fees would be in the range of 8,000 EUR per claim. In addition to the lawyer fees you need to pay court fees which will be reimbursed by the opponent when the opponent has lost the case. 

Once the case has been decided by the court, the losing party will have to reimburse also the lawyer fees but limited to the fees calculated on the basis of the German Acto on Lawyer Fees.

Hi [~accountid:616697d9048360006ac1b09b],

Please, before instructing a debt collection agency, I just want to double check that you are aware of the potential negative impact of using such an agency on the relationship with the fleet based on external counsel's analysis.

If you are fine with that, please confirm and I will promptly instruct a debt collection agency. 



FYI I am copying below the information provided by the external counsel and that I shared with [~accountid:5da43893ed16e20db5663750] regarding the options we have to recover the money:

*Option 1: Instruct a debt collection agency and let them try to obtain the money*{{.}}*The pros and cons can be briefly summarized as follows:* 

Pros:

+very specialized in debt collection

+very persistent

+most cost-effective solution – they sometimes even work on the basis of a success fee 

Cons:

-involving a debt collection agency may have a negative impact on existing client relationships (relevant if you intend to continue to work with the relevant fleets)

-the debt collection process is very much controlled by the agency; you don’t have much influence

-they cannot represent you at court, so if they are not successful you have lost time and need to instruct a lawyer anyway. 

*Option 2: Order for Payment Procedure*{{ }}*An order for payment procedure is a quick and simplified alternative to normal legal proceedings. The German order for payment procedure consist of two steps: It begins with applying for an order for payment with the competent court. This application is not comparable to a detailed statement of claim – you can use a standard form. The competent court only assesses if all formalities are met and issues an order for payment which the debtor will receive. It is then up to the debtor to react to this by either (i) paying the debt, (ii) objecting to the order for payment or (iii) remaining silent. In the event of an objection by the debtor, normal legal court proceedings follow. In the event of failure to act, an enforcement order may be issued. If the defendant objects to this, again normal legal proceedings follow. If he remains inactive, you will receive an enforcement order which is equal to a court ruling and which enables the actual debt recovery.* 

Pros:

+ Useful if you believe that the Order of Payment impresses the debtor enough so that he will finally pay. You are then much quicker than in normal court proceedings. 

Cons:

* If the debtor objects (which can be done very easily) then we will have lost time until normal proceedings start. 

*Option 3: Normal court proceedings*{{.}}*An order for payment procedures only makes sense if it is to be expected that the debtor either will pay upon such formal order received from a court or if it is likely that he remains silent. If you expect the company to refuse the return of the payment and to object to the whole proceeding then it may be recommendable to directly proceed with normal legal proceedings before the competent civil court. Normal court proceedings will take between 6-12 months.* 

If the relevant amounts aren’t low then the external counsel recommends starting normal court proceedings instead of using debt collection agencies and instead of starting this special Order for Payment Procedure.Lawyer fees would be in the range of 8,000 EUR per claim. In addition to the lawyer fees you need to pay court fees which will be reimbursed by the opponent when the opponent has lost the case. 

Once the case has been decided by the court, the losing party will have to reimburse also the lawyer fees but limited to the fees calculated on the basis of the German Acto on Lawyer Fees. 



Thank you.

{quote}1. Will an update to Bolt's Policy wording have any bearing on the consent? Answer:
*The Bolt Policy can be used as long as the below is covered:*


* The Data Subject is aware that background screening checks will be done
* Consents to Bolt that they are comfortable with the checks being processed – ie a consent form is signed / Policy acknowledged
* The checks to be done are highlighted to the Data Subject
* Information mentioned about cross border transfer
* Storage and retention of information to be noted
* That the information provide is correct and accurate
* Sharing of personal information with verification suppliers
* A formal letter is done and accepted when their a agreement (clauses) in the Data Subjects contract which gives permission for checks to be done.
* What was noticed is that the Bolt policy did not cover was purpose of the checks – ie it does not make mention that rechecks can be redone; however, whether there is consent to recheck across the board lies with the client to determine. MIE can no longer confirm what safeguards a company as ‘consent’; however, the above given as a guidelines, based on the previous form which MIE had in place which was approved by Legal and POPIA compliant.

* +10% more drivers completed a trip
* +28% increase in driver nonresponses (4% -> 5%)

* +9.2% GMV but not s.s. (p-value 0.07)

Interestingly we saw statistically significant results even one hour after the campaign ended.

* +10% finished orders
* +10% more drivers completed a trip

SQL code used for business case: 

{noformat}WITH target_phone_number AS (
SELECT 
	co.user_phone, 
	COUNT(DISTINCT co.user_id) AS count_distinct_user 
FROM 
	pii.company_order AS co 
WHERE 
	co.created >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR'
GROUP BY 1 
HAVING count_distinct_user > 2 
)	

SELECT 	
	-- tpn.count_distinct_user, 
	-- co.user_phone, 	
	-- count
	-- COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ceccu.value IS NOT NULL THEN co.id || co.city_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_event_order, 
	-- COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN crecu.value IS NOT NULL THEN co.id || co.city_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_referral_earned_order, 
	-- COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN crscu.value IS NOT NULL THEN co.id || co.city_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_referral_shared_order, 
	-- COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ctccu.value IS NOT NULL THEN co.id || co.city_id ELSE NULL END) AS count_targeted_order, 
	-- sum
	asc2.country_code, 
	COUNT(DISTINCT co.user_id) AS count_distinct_user_id, 
	ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ceccu.value IS NOT NULL THEN (ot.ride_price - ot.price)/r.rate ELSE 0 END), 0) AS sum_event_order, 
	ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN crecu.value IS NOT NULL THEN (ot.ride_price - ot.price)/r.rate ELSE 0 END), 0) AS sum_referral_earned_order, 
	ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN crscu.value IS NOT NULL THEN (ot.ride_price - ot.price)/r.rate ELSE 0 END), 0) AS sum_referral_shared_order,
	ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ctccu.value IS NOT NULL THEN (ot.ride_price - ot.price)/r.rate ELSE 0 END), 0) AS sum_targeted_order,
	sum_event_order+sum_referral_shared_order+sum_targeted_order AS total_abuse_amount 
FROM 
	pii.company_order AS co 
	LEFT JOIN admin_system_city asc2 
		ON co.city_id = asc2.id 
	LEFT JOIN target_phone_number AS tpn 
		ON co.user_phone = tpn.user_phone 
	LEFT JOIN company_order_try AS ot 
		ON co.id = ot.order_id 
		AND co.city_id = ot.city_id 
	LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r
		ON ot.price_currency = r.currency 
		AND DATE(co.created) = DATE(r.valid_on)
	-- event campaign 
	LEFT JOIN campaign_event_campaign_code_usage AS ceccu
		ON ceccu.user_id = co.user_id 
		AND ceccu.order_try_id = ot.id
	-- referral campaign - shared code (invitee)
	LEFT JOIN campaign_referral_shared_code_usage AS crscu
		ON crscu.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND crscu.order_try_id = ot.id
	-- referral campaign - earned code (inviter)
	LEFT JOIN campaign_referral_earned_code_usage AS crecu
		ON crecu.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND crecu.order_try_id = ot.id 
	-- targeted campaign 
	LEFT JOIN campaign_targeted_campaign_code_usage AS ctccu
		ON ctccu.user_id = co.user_id 
		AND ctccu.order_try_id = ot.id 
WHERE 
	tpn.count_distinct_user IS NOT NULL 
	AND co.created >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH'
	AND ot.state = 'finished'
	AND co.user_phone IS NOT NULL 
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 7 DESC {noformat}

_1.1.1.      provide any services or assistance to any person engaged or about to become engaged in the Competing Business;_

_1.1.2.      otherwise be engaged, concerned or interested, whether as a consultant, advisor, agent, representative, investor, joint venture, owner, partner (including silent partner), shareholder or in any other capacity, in the Competing Business;_

_1.1.3.      on behalf of Competing Business, be involved with the provision of goods or services or otherwise have any business dealings with any customer or prospective customer of Bolt Group with whom the Partner dealt during the Term or about whom the Partner had access to the Confidential Information;_

_1.1.4.      on behalf of Competing Business, entice or solicit, or endeavour to entice or solicit, any customer or prospective customer of Bolt Group to provide business;_

_1.1.5.     on behalf of Competing Business, have any business dealings with any person which has provided goods or services (other than utilities or administration-related supplies) to Bolt Group;_

_1.2.         If the Consultant breaches the Non-Competition Obligation Bolt may demand a contractual penalty in amount of 12000 EUR._”

But instead that consultant only wants to commit to “_Dentons Global Advisors Europe SA., may supply services to any third parties,  including Client's competitors, that are similar or identical to the Services provided that doing so does not adversely impact the quality of the Services under this Agreement._” → *Which means they would be allowed to work for any of our competitors, and provide them the same services as us, with the only limitation that this cannot adversely impact the quality of the services they are providing to us under the agreement. → At the end of the day, this is a business decision: either you are willing to engage with them even if they’ll be working for our competitors, or you are not, in which case you need to push back and ask for the usual non-competition clause I’m afraid.*

* *I understand they also want to amend the wording of clause 10 Non-Solicitation.*

We usually say that “_The Consultant shall not during the Term or for a period of 1 year 1 year after expiry or termination of this Agreement, directly or indirectly solicit or entice away from Bolt or from any Bolt Group company any employee or contractor_.”

But they would prefer to change to:

_“1.2           During this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after termination or expiration of this Agreement for whatever reason, each party undertakes that it shall not:_

_(a)            encourage any employee of the other party to end his or her relationship with that other party;_

_(b)            encourage a customer, supplier, agent or any other third party to end its relationship with that other party or breach or modify the conditions of the relationship in a way that is disadvantageous to that other party;_

_(c)             directly or indirectly, in any capacity, employ or retain the services of any employee of that other party or of any person who, at any time during the 12 months preceding the date of intended employment or retention by the undertaking party, has been an employee of that other party._

_1.3           If a party breaches this Article, that party shall pay to the other on first request a lump amount of twice the fees stated in the scope of work without prejudice to any claim the damage party may have for additional damages._

_1.4           This Article shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any termination or expiration of this Agreement.”_

*I wouldn’t recommend agreeing to this as this is rather onerous. Instead, if this is fine with you, I would propose to amend clause 10 to make it mutual, i.e.*

“None of the parties shall, during the Term and for a period of 1 year after expiry or termination of this Agreement, directly or indirectly solicit or entice away from the other party or from any of the other parties' group companies any employee or contractor.”

So no actual transactions were done between those 2 adjustments - it’s only visible on the report/balance & should be communicated with the courier that there was a mistake on our end. Hi all\!

So we have agreed on an approach from legal side that can be applied to fleet account deletion process. 

In general, the meaning of account deletion is different from the request of deleting personal data. However, account deletion should trigger the deletion of personal data (after a period which is set beforehand in the retention schedule).

We can take the following approach regarding what the FO requests:

*a) FO requests for deletion of the account*

Account deletion should mean that the account can not be retrieved - so the account would be archived (not only closed). FO should have the right to ask for the deletion of their account, however this does not automatically mean that all data should instantly also be deleted.

If the account is deleted, the personal data should be deleted after the retention period set. This can follow the logic set in our driver privacy notice: 

* all account data (including FO details and driver details) is retained for 3 years after account deletion - for possible claims, disputes arising from the agreement with the FO
* data necessary for accounting purposes is retained for 7 years

If the FO asks for the deletion of their account, then this constitutes as the termination of their agreement with Bolt. 

*b) FO requests for deleting the personal data.*

It is not possible to request deletion of personal data separately from deleting the account. 

Therefore, if such a request comes then we advise that their request means that their account will also be deleted. 

*Other questions:*

Verification of identity - if we communicate with the FO by using their provided e-mail, then account deletion request should be deemed sufficient if it comes from that e-mail as well.

h3. Testing suggestions:

* use 1 provider test account
* use 2 courier test accounts at the same position (make sure that they can have orders from your provider assigned to them) and make sure to have both of them online
* configure one of the couriers as dedicated for that provider (add its ID to assigned courier list in the courier's configuration page) and make sure that they are not marked as exclusive or test (and that the provider is not exclusive as well)
* reposition the other one to be slightly closer to the provider (a few hundred meters should suffice)
* configure the prioritisation timing buffer from the provider page ({{dedicated couriers tradeoff}}  under the {{associated courier IDs}} section in provider info tab) to something like {{600}} seconds
* use 1 eater test account and make an order from your test provider
* If everything was configured ok, then the dedicated courier, despite having a longer trip to the provider, should get assigned to the order.
* just to be safe, redo the test once more (with the same coordinates), but set the tradeoff time buffer to {{0}} and check which courier is selected; The closest courier (which is not dedicated) should be chosen over the dedicated one

*Note:* if the {{dedicated courier tradeoff}} field is empty (as in not zero, but not a value either) it will fallback to a per city courier setting value ({{matching_settings.dedicated_couriers_prioritisation.timing_buffer_seconds}}), which in turn it will fallback to 0 if not configured.

Hi David\!

As discussed with Kaspar, recording here for transparency: 

There are several options in most markets for enforcing debts- e.g. contacting the couriers ourselves, using a debt collection agency, using courts (usually there are simplified proceedings for these kinds of monetary debts), using public “debtor” pages which list the names of people who have debts (this is more of a scare tactic, not an actual way to enforce debts). 

However, before moving forward with any enforcement proceedings, it should be analysed a) what the costs of each of these options are - including both headcount costs (as probably each market would need a dedicated person to deal with the debts), as well as the external costs (state fees, legal fees etc), b) what the process is - from what amount do we enforce. 

From looking at the amount of the debt that has accrued in HR over 3 months, my initial gut feeling is that the debts for enforcing would outweigh the costs - so no benefit from now. In addition to that, actually setting up a process and mapping out costs for enforcement is would require a lot of resource (both from legal’s side as well as the business side), so the amounts currently do not justify this.

From DB perspective, MySQL just needs to grab the metadata lock on all tables being moved to new schema. This means that writes on such tables should be stopped (or very few, short ones) to give RENAME command a chance to grab the lock and move the tables. From that point on, you’ll have the two separate schemas. 

From Application perspective, after RENAME, it will stop seeing the {{vehicle*}} tables in old schema and start seeing them in new schema. Obviously, the application code needs to be able to handle this, either with specific biz logic or with stop app/rename tables/deploy new version of app that uses new schema.


- Should be {{rental_car_order}} also stopped? It uses {{taxify_rental_car_order_global}} as well, but not tables for renaming
In theory, no, only tables being moved need to be have writes stopped on. I’m not 100% sure if a {{SCHEMA}} level lock is needed. I will do some testing and let you know. 

- Or another possible solution is just to block Write operations for the server user

Yes, this should also work as read lock have lower priority.

You described several purposes for which the gender data would be collected and used. In order to start collecting this at registration, we would need to have a clear purpose on why we are doing this. 

# *Women only category as a functionality*
1.1 *Drivers gender data collection*
Here we can (at first assessment) rely on legitimate interest legal basis to start processing this data of drivers. It would be an additional functionality on our platform to enhance the security for both drivers and riders. 
The gender choice would be voluntary, meaning that only those drivers who wish to offer their services in the women only category will mark their gender. 

Few things to consider:
- we need to be transparent about the purposes which we collect the data (therefore additional information to our privacy notices should be added)
- there is always risk that someone will mark their gender as “female” but actually is not. 

*For riders gender data collection:*
- the less intrusive alternative from privacy side is to have the pop up with warning that the driver may cancel if they choose a “women only category”. Maybe from practical side not the best option. 
- snapchat is an alternative - the driver will see the snap and make their decision. We will not store the snap or at least store it for only a very limited time period. 
- rider face verification - sounds like the most intrusive alternative and we would be determining the riders gender based on biometric data processing. 
# *Marketing campaigns and measuring their success*
Here I would say that only collecting gender data solely for the purpose of measuring our campaigns success isn’t really feasible. As an alternative, is there a way to collect such analytics in an anonymised format, meaning that the gender cannot be linked to a specific user?

Hey\!

The law does not foresee an obligation to share the employee’s manager details. Therefore sharing these is not a legal obligation. 

Sharing such details can be done under:

a) consent
b) legitimate interest

Consent means that we should ask the manager first if they agree on sharing their details with a bailiff. 

Legitimate interest means that we don’t ask consent, but the bailiff proves that getting such details is essentially necessary for solving the case and justifies their legitimate interest in the exact case. 

I would advise on future cases to let the manager know and ask if they are willing to be contacted by the bailiff.

*About DUPLICATED_USER issue:*
[_summary of this thread_|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02HHFGP1BK/p1644573527129249]

* There are roughly 40-50 times a month (at least in January) that Drive Tier 2 CS handle tickets with users who have multiple driving licence verifications (for multiple accounts) (example user IDs - [337617|https://admin.bolt.eu/user/Users/user/337617], [72096995|https://admin.bolt.eu/admin/Login?from=http%3A%2F%2Fadmin.bolt.eu%2Fuser%2FUsers%2Fuser%2F72096995])
* If the actual issue is velocity/duplicate abuse, this means that the user was previously verified on another account; these verifications will clearly have a DUPLICATED_USER error stated on the verification in Admin Panel
* CS doesn’t really need access to the other account where the DL was already verified - because users cannot verify their DL for multiple accounts and that’s all there is to it (that’s why there's the 1 successful verification limitation measure in place)
* If the user changed their phone number and want to use Bolt Drive again with the new account:
** CS should ask for the old phone number - they will be able to find the other account this way
** If there are no comments on the user’s old profile about a fraudulent activity or debt and all is fine, CS will complete the verification for the user
** If the user cannot share the old phone number or says they don’t remember it, unfortunately we can do nothing
* However, if the user changed their phone number, had requested to delete their account (and it was done) and wants to verify their DL for their new account, we shouldn’t allow this.
** We should also keep a record of how often this happens - if this happens a lot, we can look into an escalation process for those users until we have a nice solution in place

Network issues problem:

* When we cannot establish connection we receive connection error exception, and we have a guarantee, that request wasn’t received at all by remote side. So we treat it as a connection error and could safely retry request later, if needed
* When we established connection and remote side closed it without sending response we got socket hang up exception. At that moment we don’t know was our request accepted or not.
* We try to mitigate hang ups by doing a single idempotent retry on a hang up. But there is a small chance, that quick retry will also receive hang up. We never had such cases before in Adyen, until we start to operate in Georgia, where we use local bank acquiring and in Georgia chances of hang up error during payment request are high
* We have 2 issues in Georgia:
** hang up on pre-order /authorise treated as technical error, order blocked, sometimes we got success notification later, need to be cancelled properly
** hang up on post-order /authorise possibly could lead to double charge, if we did authorise and then got hang up twice on capture request.
* To fix double charge I propose to:
** treat hang up as technical error only for authorise request, because notification handler have code to cancel it on success, if it was marked as error in our DB
** for capture request to Adyen, treat hang up as pending state and repeat it idempotently 3 hours later, if no notification comes at all
