We had a meeting with the Risk & Safety team (Anni Faltis) and Drive OPS (Henriko Aer, Maksim Palonen). The following questions were discussed:

* How do we currently discover potential fuel theft cases - does it come from OPS or CS?
* When do we consider the fuel card being stolen?
* How should we communicate with the user who is the potential fuel thief?
* Do we need to block the rental if there is no fuel card and no fuel?
* When do we block the user? Do we hard-block them or allow them to use other services?

All points were discussed and further action items confirmed - the checklist was updated according to what we agreed on.

----

*Discovering potential fuel cases*
Almost all fuel theft cases come from the OPS team - it isn’t CS who discover them. There may be a few reported cases where the reporter had seen someone with a Drive vehicle putting fuel into a canister. However, regular users pretty much do not care about someone stealing fuel. It is up to OPS to discover these potential fuel thieves.
The OPS team checks if the vehicle had been actually refuelled. Photos are taken when needed. We contact the customer and observe their behaviour.

*When do we consider the fuel card stolen?*
If CS escalate to OPS that a fuel card is missing from a car, OPS look for the customer who might have taken the fuel card with themselves. This customer is contacted and asked if the fuel card might be with them - if yes, then this is not considered fuel card theft. 
OPS cannot see the last time the fuel card was used - however, they can check when a vehicle was last refuelled using this card.

*How should we communicate with the potential fuel thief?*

* Our message should always be that “we have a suspicion that their account was used to steal the fuel” - we don’t want to accuse the user that they stole the fuel
* Any communication must be done by Tier 2 CS (Stealing Fuel is also a Significant risk type event)
* OPS don’t want to share data on specific amounts of fuel stolen or any other data like that with the accused user and also with the CS
* Any tickets with users asking why they received a criminal charge for fuel theft (or however the police forms the charge), only Tier 2 CS agents should handle these cases
* If more questions are asked, the response should be along the lines of "unfortunately, we cannot provide any further details at this moment. Any communication will come from the police"
* We always want to separate Bolt from the punisher (in this case, the police since there will be a criminal charge for theft)
* Relevant comments must be left on the user profile page in Admin (by Tier 2) and the OPS Case Manager (Maksim) should be looped in, too

*Do we need to block the rental?*
The Global Event Assessment Tool currently asks to block the rental in case of the Stealing Fuel HP event. However, OPS confirmed that there is no need to hide the vehicle - the Fleet OPS Specialists react quickly (within 45-60 min) and refuel the car within minutes. This is true for smaller cities like Tallinn. Additionally, even if there’s no fuel card in the car, the users can refuel the vehicle themselves and then reach out to us to coordinate the refund.
For larger cities, it may take more time for the Fleet OPS Specialists to react and refuel the car. However, OPS can adjust the minimum fuel level for the vehicles in these cities from which the vehicle will automatically be hidden.

Anni will adjust the Assessment Tool to not require blocking the rental.

*Do we hard-block the user or allow them to use other Bolt services?*
OPS have observed that users who are potential fuel thieves also have bad behaviour characteristics when using Bolt Food (requesting refunds for minor issues, mixups) - so we can block them on all platforms. This is supported by the Risk & Safety team, as well as the Legal team.

*Solving the OPS issue, not wasting time on investigations*

❗ Henriko explained that the issue to resolve is mainly the procedure of refuelling the cars. It is the operational fault that it is so easy for users to steal the fuel cards and therefore also steal the fuel. We should come up with a better process for this. Currently, the investigations take up a lot of resources on multiple teams.

Query for business case: 


{noformat}WITH target_user_id AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
	co.user_id 
FROM 
	company_order AS co
	LEFT JOIN company_order_try AS ot 
		ON co.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND co.id = ot.order_id 
	LEFT JOIN campaign_targeted_campaign_code_usage AS ctccu
		ON ctccu.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND ctccu.order_try_id = ot.id
WHERE 
	co.created >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH'
	AND ot.state = 'finished'
	AND co.company_id IS NULL 
	AND co.reseller_company_id IS NULL 
	AND ctccu.value IS NOT NULL 
),
target_user_per_alias AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
	ppu.external_id AS user_id, 
	COUNT(DISTINCT ppu2.external_id) AS user_id_same_card_alias,  
	COUNT(DISTINCT tui.user_id) AS target_user_id_same_card_alias 
FROM 
	payment_payment_method_user AS ppmu
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_user AS ppu
		ON ppmu.payment_user_id = ppu.id 
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS ppmu2 
		ON ppmu.card_alias = ppmu2.card_alias 
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_user AS ppu2 
		ON ppmu2.payment_user_id = ppu2.id 
		AND ppu2.external_id <> ppu.external_id 
	LEFT JOIN target_user_id AS tui 
		ON tui.user_id = ppu2.external_id 
WHERE 
	ppmu.is_deleted IS FALSE 
	AND ppmu.is_hidden IS FALSE 
	AND ppmu2.is_deleted IS FALSE 
	AND ppmu2.is_hidden IS FALSE 
GROUP BY 1 
ORDER BY 2 DESC 
)


SELECT 
	co.country, 
	ROUND(SUM((ot.ride_price - ot.price)/r.rate), 0) AS targeted_campaign_eur_spent 
FROM 
	company_order AS co 
	LEFT JOIN company_order_try AS ot 
		ON co.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND co.id = ot.order_id 
	LEFT JOIN campaign_targeted_campaign_code_usage AS ctccu
		ON ctccu.city_id = ot.city_id 
		AND ctccu.order_try_id = ot.id
	LEFT JOIN target_user_per_alias AS tupa 
		ON tupa.user_id = co.user_id 
	LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r
		ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(co.created)
		AND r.currency = ot.price_currency 
WHERE 
	co.created >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH'
	AND ot.state = 'finished'
	AND co.company_id IS NULL 
	AND co.reseller_company_id IS NULL 
	AND ctccu.value IS NOT NULL 
	AND tupa.target_user_id_same_card_alias > 3 
GROUP BY 1 
{noformat}

Reply from the Restaurant:

 „Dear All,

The reason to believe that the phrase "Campaign compensation" is unfortunate and should be avoided is as follows.

According to the Polish VAT Law, *the turnover for VAT purposes (which is the taxable base) is defined as anything that a taxpayer* (here: a restaurant) *receives*as the compensation for the provision of goods or services, *either directly from a purchaser or from any third party*.  The VAT Law further specifies that the compensation shall include in particular, apart from the price itself, any subsidies, grants, and additional payments of whatever kind.

In view of that, let me present an example: if the regular price is 100, the discounted price for the customer is 80, but the restaurant receives also 9,26 (10/1,08) from Bolt, then the taxable base for the restaurant is 89,26.

The fact that payments are netted off does not change that.  Under the VAT Law, if one taxpayer makes a taxable supply the value of, say, 9,26 (here: the restaurant) and the other taxpayer (here: Bolt) makes a taxable supply the value of, say, 22,5 (25% of 90), and as a result the real flow of funds is 13,24, *this DOES NOT mean that the taxpayer* (i.e. the restaurant) *is exempt from reporting 9,26 as its taxable basis*.

However, if under an alternative scenario the restaurant would not receive any compensation for the campaign, but instead Bolt would charge an effective agency fee lowered in such a way to produce the same arithmetical result (no subsidy for the restaurant), then the restaurant would not need to report the campaign compensation as its taxable base for VAT purposes.

Such a solution should be supported by both the layout of the invoice and the rules of the campaign, so that none of the documents suggested that any compensation of the restaurant is set off against Bolt’s commission.  At the same time, as the restaurant and Bolt are unrelated parties, the commission can be set completely freely: the regular commission can be 25%, while the effective commission over the campaign period may be 10% (what would be arithmetically the outcome).

In the current model (two-way settlements) Bolt protects itself by paying out the compensation for the campaign in the net amount (Bold share in discount/1+8%), but this does not solve the VAT problem for the restaurants, due to the reasons presented above.

I trust that the above comments and explanations will prove clear and helpful.

Kind regards,

Rafał Ciołek”

Hi Emilie,

ah yes, for sure. As this type of communication constitute third-party marketing, there are some legal requirements we should bear in mind. In the UE markets this type of marketing (including e-mails, text, push notifications) requires prior marketing consent, unless the communication is made in a blanket form of advertisement - e.g. the banner that every user sees. Therefore, from legal perspective, it is recommended either:

a) to conduct targeted, consent-based campaign, OR

b) to advertise those services using in-app banners, blog posts or other form of advertising that every user sees when using our services - this type of marketing doesn’t require prior consent.

*Problem or opportunity statement*

# Most of the Drive issues CS escalate to OPS via Slack.
# The current Drive issue escalation practice causes issues on all fronts:
## *For the OPS:* While this allows back and forth communication between CS and OPS, it is difficult for OPS to filter, monitor, prioritise these escalated issues and get any kind of reporting. [A deep dive|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14VTtiGUTq1bBDYapHKw3GwAIef_klelEIitk35uZclY/edit#gid=0] also showed that CS agents often tag OPS incorrectly or don’t provide all details necessary to resolve the issue without requiring back and forth comms.
## *For CS:* Since the current escalation instructions ask to either tag the Fleet OPS specialist on duty or tag a specific OPS team member (Henriko Aer, Tauno Laja, Jarmo Sõnna - often in different combinations), agents are required to always reference a KB article to know who to tag. Some of the processes also ask to create a maintenance task in Admin and then duplicate more or less the same details in Slack just to notify the OPS.
## *For CS Content:* 50% of Drive KB articles include instructions for how to correctly escalate various issues to OPS. Updating these articles requires CS Content resources that could otherwise be spent on more crucial content and process updates.
# Our own tools like Admin and the Transporter app could help simplify the CS escalation process and the OPS team’s work on resolving the reported issues. There’s plenty of room for automation, pulling data automatically, and making sure that agents provide exactly the information the OPS team needs, not requiring back and forth communication.

*Desired outcome*

* Multi-channel strategy for CS escalations to OPS:
** OPS Service Desk - low urgency requests requiring no follow-ups with the user
** Admin - escalations to Fleet OPS Specialists on duty could be submitted as Maintenance tasks
** Zendesk - routing issues that can be handled by Tier 2
** Slack - reserved for critical or unique issues, and issues that require back and forth comms between CS and OPS
* Simple and scalable instructions for CS escalations to OPS that don’t require lots of maintenance
* Clear instructions for CS what information they should include in their escalations to OPS for each issue without duplicating information in multiple platforms

*Deliverables*

# OPS Service Desk space created and migration of relevant escalations
# Escalations to Fleet OPS Specialist on duty migrated from Slack to Admin
# Tier 2 CS escalations migrated from Slack to Zendesk
# A new KB article _Drive escalation guidelines_ with clear instructions scalable across all Drive markets
# Quarterly reviews of the escalations in Drive scheduled

*Out of scope*

* Requirements for escalation migration to Admin must be provided by the OPS team (they are the ones who can determine what is needed for Fleet OPS Specialists to work effectively on the escalations in Admin and whether additional development is needed for the Transporter app).
* Information about what kind of details are missing on the CS escalation reports must come from the OPS team.

*CONTEXT*
There are *4* Pricing input methods, out of which *3* are *modifiable* and 1 is not.

{code:none}PriceModificationType (Modifiable)
STEP - There are (+) and (-) options, with which the price can be increased or decreased.
FREE INPUT - This is an Edittext, where keyboard appears on tap 
and price can be typed into along with decimal point.
FREE INPUT SHIFTING - Also an edittext, but every digit shifts towards the left 
when new digit is given as input.{code}

{code:none}PriceModificationType
NONE - Happens when `priceModificationAllowed` is false. Here the price is fixed.
NONE is generally when we don’t want to have driver editing the price (in most cases they don’t have any taximeters){code}



+Useful links+: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3700752827/Free+input+pricing|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3700752827/Free+input+pricing|smart-link] , [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mhSuQkE8GqKOtJLYb6NPLi4-871EWFqNCBWFhUKE2dA/edit#heading=h.68lhzo5sal1b|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mhSuQkE8GqKOtJLYb6NPLi4-871EWFqNCBWFhUKE2dA/edit#heading=h.68lhzo5sal1b|smart-link]  (Regarding locations where each input type is enabled)


*PRICING CATEGORIES*

* *FIXED-PRICE (Without promo)*
** This is the final price that is visible to the driver after the ride is completed. It could either be modified if the driver has a taximeter but does not include additional discounts from the rider’s side. 
* *DISCOUNT PRICE (With promo)*
** When the rider applies a promo, the original price is discounted based on the promo amount. Driver will be compensated from Bolt according to promo amount and the rest will be paid by the rider.

{color:#ff5630}*CURRENT BEHAVIOUR* {color}
We show only one screen as the Price Confirmation screen in the existing implementation.

*For Step Input method* 

      *Without Promo:* 
      Confirm Price Screen is shown

      Display the text hint - Enter the price indicated on the taximeter (applicable for all modifiable input types,i.e having taximeter)
      Price input type is Step (+/-)

      Display Payment type message label below
      Display other details if available - Problem with Price, Toll roads, Recalculation reason, etc.

      On Confirm button swiped, proceed to Rate Client if possible.

      *With Promo*

      Apply Promo for Rider and make a ride. 

      On end ride, Confirm Price screen appears

      In Addition to what is displayed in ‘Without Promo’ case, we can see the following

      Trip with Compensation label

      Promo details section showing, Promo amount compensated by Bolt and Total fare -> Price on taximeter + Promo amount

      Here on changing the price, in the modification section on the top, the Total fare is also changed accordingly.

      *Problem Faced*: Drivers cannot understand clearly if the amount to be collected is the one on the top that is modifiable by the driver(or the one that is just displayed when Price modification is not allowed) or if it is the total fare to be collected.

      *Landscape Orientation*

      Price is displayed (modifiable or fixed) in the bottom left. To its right Confirm Price Button is present

----

      *For Free Input method*

      *Without promo*

      In portrait orientation, the keyboard is shown initially and when text is empty in the price input section, currency hint(0💶  ) is displayed.

      Price is entered using keyboard and on orientation change, the price is still displayed and is not reset to 0 or empty edit- text.

      On Set Price Button Tapped, a confirmation dialog appears prompting to confirm the final price. On clicking Confirm button, the dialog proceeds to Rate client. If the Cancel button is clicked, dialog is dismissed and Set price comes into visibility again.

      *With Promo*

      Confirm Price screen similar to Step input with promo is displayed 🤔 

----

      *For Free Input Shift method*

      
      *Without promo*

      Same as the previous cases, except that the input method shifts to left for each number typed.

      *With promo*

       Same as With Promo - Free input case

----

h3. {color:#36b37e}*NEW IMPLEMENTATION OF REDESIGNED PRICE CONFIRMATION SCREENS*{color}

We will be splitting the single confirmation screen into two screens - *Set Price Screen* and *Confirm Price Screen*

When {{PriceModificationType}}- *NONE ,*  there is only a single screen - Confirm Price Screen. Set Price screen should not be shown.

*SET PRICE Screen* 

Allows the driver to enter the price displayed on the taximeter (if the price is modifiable by the driver) otherwise, Driver can only see the price allotted for the ride (Price modification disabled case).

The screen has Only the following data

* Price of the ride
* Enter the price indicated on the taximeter label(if price modifiable)
* SET PRICE Button

On ‘Set Price’ Button clicked, Confirm price screen is opened.

+*SET PRICE SCREEN Behaviour*+

      *For Step Input:*

      *Without Promo:*

      Display the  price with (+/-) step modification view if the price is modifiable

      If the price can’t be modified, only display the Price without (+/-)     

      Rest of the UI is just as mentioned above 

----

      *For Free Input:*

      *Without Promo:*

      Price input type should be edit-text where the decimal point should also be entered by the driver. 

      The keyboard is displayed initially in Portrait mode. On tapping on the edit-text, the keyboard appears. The Set Price Button should translate above the keyboard and not stay hidden behind the keyboard.

      On orientation change, the price entered should be maintained and, not be reset to 0 or be empty.

----

    *For Free Input Shifting:*

      *Without Promo:*

      Same as Free Input except that the input method shifts to left for each number typed.

      On orientation change, the price entered should be maintained and, not be reset to 0 or be empty.

----

    *Landscape Orientation for Set Price Screen*

    The Price Input view stays on the top just like in Portrait. Only the Set Price Button is fixed to the bottom of the screen.

     *With Promo case for Set Price Screen:*

      *No UI related to Promo in Set Price screen*. Price view is displayed with the original price of the ride (without applying promo discount). Hence it can also be modified by the driver marginally as indicated on the taximeter. So the Set price screen is as simple as possible.

      *No Dialog appears after Set Price Button tap for Free Input / Shifting types. Hence, the dialog can be removed and on the Set price button tap, it navigates to confirm the price screen.*

----

*CONFIRM PRICE SCREEN*

This screen appears when Set Price Button is tapped on the previous screen

Confirm Price Screen has the following UI

*Without Promo*

* Price of the ride - (info about the calculation of the price displayed is stated below)
* Payment method type label (Cash/ Bolt payment etc)
* Problem with price section (if price review allowed)
* Toll roads, price recalculation reason, etc.
* Confirm Price Swipe Button. 

*With Promo*

* In addition to the above UI, it also contains Promo related section - Compensated by Bolt, Total Fare.

*PRICE CANNOT BE MODIFIED ON THIS SCREEN.* To make changes to the input price, there is a Back Button on the title bar. On clicking Back, the Set Price screen appears. 

If the price was modified by the driver and was set earlier, the modified price should be displayed and not the initial price

On Confirm Button Swiped, it proceeds to Rate Client screen if possible

*Landscape Orientation*

It has the price on the top and only the Confirm Button is fixed to the bottom of the screen. Rest of the content scrolls behind.

----

*PRICE COMPUTATION FOR PROMO CASE*

On the Set Price screen , the driver will not be aware of the promo discount amount. He will only enter the price on the taximeter.

When navigated to Confirm Price screen, the Price displayed as Preview will be the amount after promo is applied.

The promo discount amount will be shown next to 'Bolt will compensate you' text

Total fare = Computed price (actual price) + Promo Amount 

Few examples:

Base Rider Price / Original Price before promo applied = *10*

Promo amount = *3* 

In Rider app we can see price as :   *-10-*  *7*

What appears on the Driver App - 

Set Price Screen : *10 (original price of the ride)*  (Price can be modified by the driver - ‘delta’  (+/-))

Confirm Price Screen

Price Preview :  *7* + delta (Actual price -> 10 - 3 + delta)

Bolt will compensate you : *3*

Total Fare : *10*

*Another Example*

Original Price : 3, Promo Price : 3 

Confirm Price Screen : 

Price Preview - 0 , Bolt will compensate you - 3 , Total Fare - 3

*What if the driver modifies the price LOWER than the promo discount price?*

Price can never be negative, min price is *zero.* So for the following case,

Original Price : 3, Promo Price : 3 , Actual Price - 2 (Price modified by driver using modification types in Set Price screen)

Confirm Price Screen : 

Price Preview - 0 , Bolt will compensate you - 2, Total Fare - 2

*PRICE CAN NEVER BE SET TO 0 IN SET PRICE SCREEN, if price is zero and Set Price Button is tapped, display “*{color:#ff5630}*Error with Price*{color}*” label. After this ,it cannot navigate to Confirm Price screen*

----

+_In case of Bolt, the letter from CPO is based on article 49a – soft inquiry. Lack of response should not generate any legal consequences to Bolt._+

_In case official requests (based on article 50) lack of fulfilment of such request may result, in worst case scenario, even in imposing an administrative penalty in amount up to EUR 50 million._

_While contemplating whether to respond or not, please take into consideration future relation with CPO. From our experience lack of fulfilment of such soft-inquiry may result in hindering relation with CPO._

+_We recommend to:_+

_(i)               verify internally previous correspondence with CPO in this case; according to the letter it is a continuance of correspondence dated back March 2021 r.;_

_(ii)              prepare the short answers and divide information on two category: publicly available and confidential; if needed;_
